name: Nevua Booking
author: nevuateam

sections.description:
Nevua Booking turns your WordPress site into your booking desk. Clients pick a service and a time, and get a confirmation by email with the booking ready to add to their calendar. You see your day, your week and every booking from one screen in wp-admin.

It suits any business that works by appointment: studios, salons, consultants, classes, repairs, clinics, tutors.

What is included

  • A booking form for any page: add the Booking form block (pages, site templates and widget areas) or the [nevua_booking] shortcode. It takes your theme’s font and adapts to the width it is given, from a full-width page to a narrow sidebar.
  • The Booking Form page: a template, your brand color, font and corners, what the form shows and your own fields, with a live preview of the real form.
  • Services and working hours: durations, prices and breaks between appointments; a different schedule for each weekday, with breaks such as lunch; days off; and how early and how far ahead clients can book (two hours’ notice unless you change it).
  • Custom fields: ask clients exactly what you need.
  • Confirm at once or approve each booking: your choice. Waiting clients are told their request was received, and get the confirmation when you confirm it.
  • Emails that do the work: confirmation with a calendar file (.ics), reminder, cancellation, and a notice for you on each new booking.
  • Clients reschedule or cancel on their own, from a link in their emails, up to the notice you set.
  • Your day at a glance: today’s bookings around your working hours, the free time left, and the week’s load.
  • Bookings: upcoming first and grouped by day, or by any period you pick, exported as a spreadsheet. Confirm, reschedule, cancel, or mark a past booking as attended or as a no-show. Book a client yourself, even one who gave you no email.
  • Paid at the visit or ahead by Pix: show clients your Pix key or bank details to pay before the session, and mark a booking paid, with how it was paid. Prices are in the currency you choose in Settings.
  • Answers checked as they are typed: phone and your country’s tax id are masked, and email is checked, in the form and again on the server. Tax ids: CPF or CNPJ (Brazil), RUT (Chile), CUIT or DNI (Argentina), CI or RUT (Uruguay), DNI or RUC (Peru), C.C. or NIT (Colombia), RFC (Mexico).
  • No spam bookings, no puzzle: an invisible check turns away booking robots, and each visitor can book only a few times a minute.
  • Privacy tools: a client’s bookings are included in WordPress’s export and erase personal data tools.
  • Languages: the admin screens and the booking form come in English, Portuguese (Brazil) and Spanish. Emails and the other texts follow your site’s language as its translations reach translate.wordpress.org.

Nevua Booking PRO

An optional paid upgrade adds online payments (Stripe, PayPal and Mercado Pago, including Pix), deposits, session packages, a waitlist, receipts, several professionals with their own schedules, locations, WhatsApp and SMS notifications, online meeting links, Google Calendar and Outlook sync, weekly series of bookings and reports. None of it is needed to take bookings with this plugin. See wpnevua.com for PRO.

External services

This plugin connects to one external service:

  • Freemius (freemius.com) handles the plugin’s licensing, its upgrade and its updates for PRO.
    • Only if you opt in when you activate the plugin, Freemius receives your name and email, your site’s address, language and IP, the WordPress, PHP and plugin versions, and, if you allow it, the list of your plugins and themes. It is used to send you security and feature updates and to improve the plugin. Skip the opt-in and none of this is sent; you can opt out later with the Opt Out link under Nevua Booking on the Plugins screen.
    • The upgrade page (Nevua > Plan > Upgrade to PRO) asks Freemius for the current PRO prices, about once a day. It sends only your site’s address (in the request’s header), nothing about you or your clients.
    • When you deactivate the plugin, Freemius may ask why. Only if you answer, the reason you picked is sent; without the opt-in it goes with an anonymous id, not your name or email.
    • Terms of service, privacy policy.

Bookings, clients and settings stay in your WordPress database.

Source code

The admin screens and the booking form are Vue apps. The minified JavaScript and CSS in dist/ are built from the human-readable source in src/, which ships with the plugin, together with package.json, bun.lock and the Vite, TypeScript, Tailwind and PostCSS configuration.

To build it yourself:

  1. Install Bun (or use npm).
  2. In the plugin folder, run bun install, then bun run build.

The build writes dist/, the same files the plugin loads.
sections.installation:
1. Install the plugin from the Plugins screen (Plugins > Add New Plugin), or upload it to /wp-content/plugins/nevua-booking.
  2. Activate it.
  3. Open the Nevua menu to set up your services and working hours.
  4. Add the booking form to any page: in the block editor, insert the Booking form block (it can also open straight at one service). Elsewhere, use the shortcode [nevua_booking].
sections.faq:
Is it compatible with my theme?

Yes. The booking form uses your theme’s font, fills the width of the area you place it in and adjusts its layout to that width. Its colors come from the Form Customizer.

Do clients need an account?

No. They book with their name and email. The emails they receive carry a private link to reschedule or cancel.

How do WhatsApp messages work? (PRO)

WhatsApp delivers the messages a business starts only as templates Meta approved. Nevua sends them through Twilio: create each template (confirmation, reminder, cancellation, waitlist offer) in Twilio’s Content Template Builder, wait for its approval, then enter its Content SID and the values it uses under Notifications > Messages > WhatsApp, where a suggested text and a test send are ready. Only the values you map go to WhatsApp, never the client’s email or phone.

Reminders arrive late, or not at all

WordPress runs scheduled tasks, such as reminders, only when someone visits your site, and not at all when WP-Cron is switched off. The dashboard’s System status shows when reminders last ran and warns when they are late. For reminders on time, ask your host for a real cron job that calls wp-cron.php every few minutes.

Clients don’t receive the emails

Nevua sends email through WordPress, which on many hosts uses the server’s own mail and often lands in spam or is dropped. Install an SMTP plugin, such as WP Mail SMTP or FluentSMTP, connected to your email provider, and use a sender address on your site’s domain (Notifications page). The dashboard’s System status lists the emails WordPress could not send in the last 7 days, with the mail server’s reason.

What happens to my bookings if I delete the plugin?

They are kept, so reinstalling brings everything back. To erase all of Nevua’s data when the plugin is deleted, turn on “Delete all data when the plugin is deleted” in Settings, then delete the plugin from the Plugins screen. With WP-CLI, run the uninstall as an administrator (wp plugin uninstall nevua-booking --user=<admin>), or the data is kept.

My site is behind Cloudflare or a proxy

Nevua limits how often one visitor can book, by their IP address. By default it uses the address your server reports, which a host that sits behind a proxy usually corrects already. If every visitor shows the proxy’s address instead, add add_filter('nevua_trust_proxy_headers', '__return_true'); (a load balancer or proxy that sets X-Forwarded-For) and, behind Cloudflare, also add_filter('nevua_trust_cloudflare', '__return_true'); to a small plugin or your theme’s functions.php. Turn these on only when the proxy is really there: otherwise a visitor could write their own address.

Which languages are included?

The admin screens and the booking form come in English, Portuguese (Brazil) and Spanish. Emails and the other texts follow your site’s language through the translations on translate.wordpress.org.
sections.changelog:
1.4.0

  • A booking keeps the price it was booked at: changing a service’s price later no longer changes what its emails, receipts and “Mark as paid” show.
  • Settings is split into General and Schedule, the working hours are one row per day (also in the professional’s dialog), and Save stays at the foot of a long tab and says when something isn’t saved yet.
  • Saving General or Schedule no longer sends back the calendar apps’ credentials read when the page opened, so it can’t empty or undo ones just saved in Calendar sync. Settings that fail to load offer Try again instead of showing defaults that could be saved over yours.
  • “Add another shift” starts where the day’s last shift ends, so it never overlaps one.
  • Fields, switches and checkboxes in the admin have edges you can see (3:1 contrast). On phones, admin fields are 16px, so iPhones no longer zoom in on them, and booking details, the dashboard week and System status fit the screen.
  • The Form Customizer has Style and Sections tabs, and picking a template keeps the preview where it was. The List layout now also lists locations and professionals one per row.
  • On a narrow form, a service’s price moves to its own line instead of running under the arrow.
  • Two booking forms on one page work independently, payment included.
  • The confirm link in a reminder waits for the client’s tap, and a move from the client’s page is checked against the booking as it is at that moment.
  • On PRO, Notifications has four tabs: Email, SMS and WhatsApp, Messages, and Logs. The message log is a list on phones.
  • On PRO, Session packages and Waitlist are tabs on the Bookings page. A waitlist offer opens the form on the professional the client waited for, and a package’s first session is rounded the way the currency is (whole pesos in CLP and COP).
  • On PRO, a phone number written without its country code is read with your currency’s country.
  • On PRO, Reports that fail to load say so with Try again, never another period’s figures, and can’t be exported.

1.3.2

  • The dashboard’s week draws a ring only on a day with bookings; an empty week shows just its days.
  • Tabs that don’t fit on a phone (Settings, Notifications) show an arrow to the rest.
  • The booking form gives a long service, professional or location name two lines; anything still cut, there or in the admin, shows whole under the mouse pointer.
  • Services, and Professionals and Locations on PRO: Delete shows on the row under the mouse; on touch screens it stays in sight.
  • Upgrading from Free offers every plan (1, 5 or 25 sites) even when the prices can’t be loaded: the button then opens the plans on wpnevua.com, not a checkout fixed on one site.
  • The opt-in and license screens show Nevua’s icon instead of a generic plug.
  • On PRO, the license screen: no ring left around a button after a click, the license dialog’s own words in your language and its fields lined up, and tidier rows on a phone.
  • On PRO, paying online: the payment methods are one quiet switch, the card is called a card (also on the confirmation, “Paid with card”), and waiting for a Pix shows as a plain line instead of a yellow block.
  • On PRO, Reports show revenue as one column per month, so no money is drawn between months, and a calmer booking status ring.
  • On PRO, the message log searches by phone or by the client’s name or email, and says how many messages it holds.
  • On PRO with PayPal: a payment PayPal reverses (a buyer’s dispute won) cancels its booking without telling the client it was refunded, and one PayPal reports some other way shows in System status. Add PAYMENT.CAPTURE.REVERSED to the events of your PayPal webhook.

1.3.1

  • System status shows the emails WordPress could not send, with the mail server’s reason; on PRO, also the calendar events and online meetings that could not be made.
  • A field with a problem keeps its red border under the mouse pointer, and a field you are typing in keeps its focus color.
  • The booking form’s title is a second-level heading, so it no longer competes with the page’s own title.
  • “Upgrade” in the menu and on the Plugins screen, on Free and PRO alike; hidden when no bigger plan exists. The license is changed from the Plan page.
  • “Pix” spelled as the Central Bank of Brazil writes it.
  • Simpler code inside, and the booking and payment flows tested on every change.

1.3.0

  • First public release on WordPress.org.
  • A booking form block and shortcode that fit your theme, with a Booking Form page to style it and your own fields.
  • Working hours for each weekday with breaks, days off, and how early and how far ahead clients can book.
  • Emails with calendar files, and a private link for clients to confirm, reschedule or cancel.
  • Pay at the visit or ahead by Pix or bank details, in the currency you choose; bookings exported as a spreadsheet.
  • An invisible check against booking robots.
  • Admin screens and booking form in English, Portuguese (Brazil) and Spanish.
